name: Caquetio
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct, essentially unattested (Aruba/Venezuela Arawakan, names and scraps only); nothing describing its phonology exists.

sources.citation: Diario (Aruba), 15 Aug 2019, 'Linguista Todd Dandaré: Caquetio no a muri completamente' (Biblioteca Nacional Aruba clipping)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; mentions a ~300-item list of Caquetío-origin words by Miguel Enrique Zavala Reyes ('Palabras vivas de una lengua muerta: legado arawak-caquetio').

sources.citation: Dutch Wikipedia, 'Caquetío (taal)' (secondary; summarises van Buurt 2015 and van Buurt & Joubert 1997; bibliography)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Its 'Fonologie' section (citing van Buurt 2015: 27) discusses only the frequency of /ʃi/ syllables and retained /w/ in Papiamentu substrate words; nothing on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Oliver, José R. 1989. The archaeological, linguistic and ethnohistorical evidence for the expansion of Arawakan into northwestern Venezuela and northeastern Colombia. PhD diss., University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The only modern scholarly treatment of the Caquetío linguistic evidence (compares the Aruba wordlists and chronicle words with Lokono/Wayuu); the one place a linguist might have remarked on accent in the attested forms, though the data almost certainly cannot support a stress statement.

sources.citation: Alfredo Jahn. 1927. Los aborígenes del occidente de Venezuela: su historia, etnografía y afinidades lingüísticas. Caracas: Lit. y Tip. del Comercio (Caquetío chapter pp. ~205-215)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. States 'no se han conservado vocabularios caquetíos' (p. 213) and lists six words from Oviedo (boratío, cazá, datihao/diao, mazato, tara, coroata) in n. 29 to argue Arawak affiliation.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid record arub1238 (Caquetio); Glottolog's most extensive descriptions = van Koolwijk 1882, Federmann 1916 [1577], Cei 1992 [1539-53], all typed a wordlist or less; no grammar/phonology/sketch
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; bibliographic record only, confirms no descriptive source beyond wordlists.

sources.citation: Nicolás Federmann. 1916 [1557]. Narración del primer viaje de Federmann a Venezuela, trad. y notas de Pedro M. Arcaya. Caracas: Lit. y Tip. del Comercio
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnohistorical narrative; Arcaya's footnote (pp. 27-28) states that the place-names are the 'únicos restos que subsisten de su idioma'.

sources.citation: Albert S. Gatschet. 1885. The Aruba language and the Papiamento jargon. Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society 22(120): 299-305 (Pinart's 1882 Aruba material pp. 300-302)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. ~14 words/phrases, toponyms, plant/animal names and six conjurer's formulas obtained by Pinart from aged natives (language abandoned since c. 1800); Gatschet remarks only on reduplication and that 'some rhythm resembling assonance is perceptible' in one formula; a couple of formula words carry an apostrophe (datie', gidio') that is not explained.

sources.citation: A. J. van Koolwijk. 1882. De Indianen Caraïben van het eiland Aruba (West-Indië). Tijdschrift van het Aardrijkskundig Genootschap 6: 222-229 (language notes and ~20-item wordlist pp. 226-227)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Says the language is no longer spoken, replaced by Papiamentu; gives ~20 words/phrases recalled 'met moeite' by old people, plus place/mountain/cave names, with Dutch-orthography diacritics (ë, ö, oe) but no stress marks or any remark on accent.

sources.citation: English Wikipedia 'Caquetío language'; Spanish Wikipedia 'Idioma caquetío'; Wikidata Q5037179
sources.note: Nothing; en-wiki notes only short wordlists (van Koolwijk 1880, Pinart 1882) survive; es-wiki is a two-sentence stub with no references.

sources.citation: Zavala Reyes, Miguel Enrique. n.d. Palabras vivas de una lengua muerta: legado arawak-caquetío (article; ~300-word list, per Diario 15 Aug 2019).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Reported ~300-item list of Caquetío-derived words from the Venezuelan side (Falcón); would enlarge the corpus though it is substrate lexicon, not a description.

sources.citation: van Buurt, Gerard. 2015. Caquetío Indians on Curaçao during colonial times and Caquetío words in the Papiamentu language.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: Most recent dedicated study of Caquetío lexical remains; has a phonology discussion (p. 27 per nl-wiki) — would confirm whether anything is said about accent in substrate words.

sources.citation: van Buurt, Gerard & Sidney M. Joubert. 1997. Stemmen uit het verleden: Indiaanse woorden in het Papiamentu. Willemstad, Curaçao: Joubert. ISBN 99904-0-145-4.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Fullest collection of Caquetío-origin words in Papiamentu with etymological notes; could carry remarks on the accentuation of borrowed forms.
